deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous page adjusts the directions at the 'Hauptpunkte der Kurhessischen Messungen'. The points are numbered as follows. 1 Göttingen Sternwarte, 2 Meridianzeichen, 3 Hohehagen, 4 Hils, 5 Brocken, 6 Meisner, 7 Inselsberg, 8 Knill, 9 Milseburg, 10 Taufstein, 11 Orberreisig, 12 Johannisberg, 13 Bergerwarte, 14 Dünsberg, 15 Amöneburg, 16 Hohelohr, 17 Hasse(…). Points 18–21 are named only in fragments in the margin. This page is the computational sequel: plane triangles, then plane rectangular coordinates of all points. The scheme ties Gerling's Kurhessian net to the Hannover net, with origin at the Göttingen observatory. The left-margin fragments are the third column of the facing page, visible at the edge.

(A) TRIANGLE SOLUTIONS (upper part, three columns of 3-line blocks). Each block lists, for one triangle:
- the three angles A_i (plane angles);
- log sin A_i, to 7 places, with Gauss's eighths, fourths and halves of the last unit;
- log of the side opposite each angle.
In the middle and right columns the vertex number is written before each angle.
The angles of every triangle sum to 180°0'0.0000" within ±0.0001", so there is no spherical excess. They are differences of plane azimuths. Example: triangle 1,2,3:
- 180°0'5.4710" − 64°1'17.5943" = 115°58'47.8767";
- 48°19'42.1407" − 0°0'5.4710" = 48°19'36.6697";
- 244°1'17.5943" − 228°19'42.1407" = 15°41'35.4536".
Sides follow from the sine rule in logarithmic form [my notation]: log b = log a − log sin A + log sin B. Example: 3.7002053 (side 1–2, the starting side) − 9.4321446 + 9.9537342 = 4.2217949 (side 2–3), and + 9.8732915 = 4.1413522 (side 1–3).
The triangles are chained, using sides already found:
- (1,2,3); (2,3,4); (3,4,5); (3,5,7) with side 5–7 = 5.0252103½; (3,6,7); (1,3,6);
- (6,7,8), (6,8,9)/(7,8,9) etc. into the Kurhessian points;
- (6,8,16), (8,15,16), (8,10,15), (8,9,10), (10,14,15), (14,15,17), (15,16,17), (16,17,18), (6,16,19), (6,19,20), (19,20,21), (10,11,12), (10,12,14), (11,12,13), …

(B) AZIMUTHS. On the previous page, line i→j and line j→i carry small final entries ±v (e.g. 1→2: −0.0162, 2→1: +0.0162). The azimuths here equal the adjusted direction plus v/2. This makes forward and back azimuths differ by exactly 180°. Examples:
- 1→2: 5.4791 − 0.0081 = 5.4710, and 2→1: 5.4629 + 0.0081 = 5.4710;
- 1→3: 17.5921 + 0.00225 = 17.5943, and 3→1: 17.5966 − 0.00225 = 17.5943.
This is my inference, but it checks on every line tested.

(C) COORDINATES (lower left). For each line from a known point P to a new point Q the row gives: azimuth α, log s, Δx = s cos α, Δy = s sin α. The system is Gauss's Hannover convention: origin at the Sternwarte, x positive south, y positive west, α counted from south through west. This is consistent with Hils lying N, Brocken NE, Inselsberg SE and Meisner SSW, in metres (Göttingen–Brocken ≈ 55.4 km).
- 1→2: (−5014.239, −0.133).
- 3 via 1: (6065.394, 12447.782); via 2: −5014.239 + 11079.636 = 6065.397.
- 1→6: (33670.285, 6065.227); via 3: 6065.394 + 27604.893 = 33670.287.
- 4 via 2: (−40946.811, 7668.266); via 3: (−40946.808, 7668.266).
- 5 via 3: (−30304.516, −46418.654); via 4: (−30304.512, −46418.647).
- 7 via 3: (75239.295, −36849.852); via 5: (75239.292, −36849.846); via 6: (75239.266, −36849.852).
The chain continues to 8, 9, 10, 11, 15, 16, 19, 20, each point reached from two or three known points as a check. Examples:
- 8 via 6 = (67981.231, 36622.185), via 7 = (67981.235, 36622.175);
- 9 via 6/7/8 = (109452.05, 3153.71…3153.73);
- 10 via 8/9 = (112298.53, 49963.07).

(D) LOG-ERROR CORRECTION. In triangle (3,6,7) the log sin of 22°27'26.64" and the side 6–7 are overwritten (…593, …149). The original side was evidently 4.7763509, i.e. 360 units of the 7th place too large. Later triangles were already built on 4.7763509, hence the notes 'Corr. aller folgenden Logg −360' and 'Corr. alle folg. Logg −360'. All logs written below the note are uncorrected, but the Δx, Δy were computed with the corrected values. Verification:
- 6→8: √(34310.946² + 30556.958²) = 45945.28, log 4.6622409 = 4.6622769 − 0.0000360;
- 14→17: √(32018.597² + 701.861²) gives log 4.505506 ≈ 4.5055426 − 0.0000360.

(E) LOWER RIGHT. These are coordinate differences between Kurhessian point pairs (10.11, 10.12, …, 20.21), each with azimuth, log distance, Δx, Δy. They serve to compute and check the remaining points. Example: x13 − x12 from 11.13 and 11.12 = 2725.630 + 20129.753 = 22855.383, matching 12.13.
errors: Gauss's own slip, corrected by him: log sin 22°27'26.64" (triangle 3,6,7) was first wrong by 360 units of the 7th decimal. This propagated to side 6–7 (4.7763509 instead of 4.7763149) and to all later triangle logs, hence the marginal 'Corr. … −360'. The logs printed afterwards remain uncorrected; the coordinate differences use corrected values.

Row 12.13 (azimuth 358°54'29.0170"): Δy is written '+435.629', but sin α < 0 there. The coordinates from 11.12 and 11.13 give y13 − y12 = −435.628, so the sign should be minus. This is a sign slip or an ambiguous mark; the magnitude is correct.

Point 7 (Inselsberg) via 6 gives x = 75239.266, against 75239.295 and 75239.292 via 3 and via 5. The 0.03 m disagreement suggests the overwritten Δx = 41568.981 (6→7) is slightly off (expected ≈ 41569.01). Δy agrees to 0.006 m.
Other multiple-route closures agree to a few millimetres, consistent with 7-place logarithms.

results.what: Solution of plane triangles of a geodetic net by the logarithmic sine rule, the angles being differences of plane azimuths so that each triangle sums to exactly 180°
results.modern_name: Plane triangulation computation (sine rule, log tables)

results.what: Making forward and back azimuths exactly reciprocal by applying half of the small discrepancy to each before computing coordinates
results.modern_name: Reduction of directions to plane grid azimuths / reciprocal azimuth adjustment

results.what: Rectangular coordinates (x south, y west, origin Göttingen observatory) from azimuth and distance, Δx = s cos α, Δy = s sin α, each point computed from two or three known points as a control
results.modern_name: Traverse/polar coordinate computation in a national grid (Gauss's Hannover system)

results.what: Linking Gerling's Kurhessian triangulation (Knill, Milseburg, Taufstein, Dünsberg, Amöneburg …) to the Hannover net through Meisner, Inselsberg, Brocken, Hils and Hohehagen
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and C. L. Gerling (collaboration known from their correspondence and Gerling's publications)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine geodetic bookkeeping: logarithmic triangle solutions and coordinate computation in Gauss's known Göttingen-origin system for the Hannover–Kurhessen junction. Gauss's collaboration with Gerling is documented. The only notable details are the self-detected 360-unit log error and the reciprocal-azimuth averaging.
